title: Dawn to dark
rule: Twelve views of the same cupboard wall across one day; the incident fills one of them, light and clock change in all.
declares: E0-E3 compressed into the 4 pm view
made: one cupboard wall built once as a HANDMADE cut model (b1m2 clock, cupboard opening on its left jamb, SERVICE door, ticket window, desk; plus a pendant lamp and a timetable board cut here) and printed twelve times as stencils in flat dyes by the page-08 method (one cut stencil per colour with paper ties, fixed misregistration, mottled dye pooling at the edges) on the LoC 1934 sheet

the day's light as two more stencils per view: a window-sun patch (two-by-two panes, sheared by the sun's height, its glazing bars left as ties) that crosses the wall from high right at dawn to high left at sunset, printed in its own tint (rose, ochre, madder; none at noon); and a shade veil cut with that patch (and after 8 p.m. the lamp's glow) as reserves, its dye and strength set per hour from dawn blue through noon umber and evening madder to night indigo
the wall clock cut to each view's time: 5:40, 7:00, 8:30, 10:00, 11:30 a.m., 1:30, 4:10, 5:20, 6:20, 7:10, 8:10, 9:30 p.m.; each view carries its time on a pasted slip in the shared pen hand

the incident only in the 4:10 view (wide, closer): memo on the desk, the stranger behind the TICKET OFFICE glass with the question and the thanks, the agent under the clock at 4:10 with the answer, the agent again at the open cupboard with the forgetting line (continuous narration in one view)
after 4:10 the cupboard stands open in every view with the ANRC 1922 key cutout (printed as an ochre stencil) on its hook, tagged SERVICE; the SERVICE door is shut in all twelve

events.E0: view 7 (4:10): the memo slip on the desk at the left; the agent has crossed the office
events.E1: view 7: 'Pardon me - have you the right time?' from the stranger behind the ticket window
events.E2: view 7: the agent under the clock (4:10): 'Ten past four, by the clock.'
events.E4: view 7: the agent at the open cupboard, the key on its hook tagged SERVICE
events.E5: view 7: pencil to his chin, 'Well, here I am... and what for?'; views 8-12: the cupboard left open, key on its hook, SERVICE door shut, till 9:30 p.m.

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: one fixed portrait view of the cupboard wall held while the day runs: the sun patch slides and the light warms, the clock moves on; at 4:10 the agent opens the cupboard and, a minute later, forgets; the light reddens and goes to night under the lamp, the cupboard still open and the key still hanging
beat_frames: b01: 5:40 a.m., dawn blue, patch high right
b03: 11:30 a.m., patch low on the cupboard
b05: 4:10 p.m., the agent swings the cupboard leaf
b06: 4:11 p.m., key on its hook, pencil to chin, the forgetting line
b07: 6:20 p.m., madder evening, cupboard open, nobody
b08: 9:30 p.m., night indigo, lamp lit, key still hanging

self_check.outcome: key on its hook and SERVICE door shut in every view after 4:10
self_check.check: Light and clock change in every panel; the incident happens in only one.
self_check.pending: independent blind reading not run by the maker
